headline: Tesla's second-gen Roadster gets official debut date after nearly a decade
summary: After years of delays, Tesla has set October 10 for the official reveal of its second-gen Roadster. The hypercar was initially promised to hit 0-60 mph in under 2 seconds with over 600 miles of range.
details: Tesla has officially announced October 10 as the reveal date for its second-generation Roadster, nearly a decade after its initial prototype debut. This commitment follows a long history of delays for the all-electric hypercar.

The original prototype, unveiled in 2017, boasted impressive specifications. Tesla claimed it would accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in under two seconds, achieve a top speed exceeding 250 mph, and offer a range of over 600 miles.

The company's website features a countdown to the reveal, teasing an image that hints at cold-gas thrusters for a 'SpaceX model' variant, potentially enabling a 'flying' capability. This ambitious feature has generated both excitement and skepticism.

Initial pricing for the Roadster's base model was set at $200,000, with a Founder's Edition at $250,000. Despite a $50,000 reservation deposit, some early pre-order holders, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and tech YouTuber Marques Brownlee, have reportedly canceled their reservations due to the prolonged wait.
caption:
Tesla's second-gen Roadster, first seen in 2017, finally has an official reveal date: October 10.

Tesla has officially announced October 10 as the reveal date for its second-generation Roadster, nearly a decade after its initial prototype debut. This commitment follows a long history of delays for the all-electric hypercar.

The original prototype, unveiled in 2017, boasted impressive specifications. Tesla claimed it would accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in under two seconds, achieve a top speed exceeding 250 mph, and offer a range of over 600 miles.

The company's website features a countdown to the reveal, teasing an image that hints at cold-gas thrusters for a 'SpaceX model' variant, potentially enabling a 'flying' capability. This ambitious feature has generated both excitement and skepticism.

Initial pricing for the Roadster's base model was set at $200,000, with a Founder's Edition at $250,000. Despite a $50,000 reservation deposit, some early pre-order holders, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and tech YouTuber Marques Brownlee, have reportedly canceled their reservations due to the prolonged wait.
